title: Add Closed Hover Micro Animations to Every Icon
description: Add a hover-triggered micro animation to every icon in the UI. Trigger on hovering the icon itself or its enclosing interactive control (button, link, menu item, tab, etc.). Play once per hover-enter. Every animation must be closed: first keyframe equals last keyframe (rest -> motion -> identical rest), so it ends seamlessly and is loopable. Give every one of the 144 vendored Lucide icons (plus 10 more to be vendored: app-window, square-dashed, redo-2, undo-2, edit-3, align-left, list-ordered, text-cursor, clipboard, file) a bespoke, semantically fitting closed keyframe animation, keyed off the existing data-icon attribute on the central Icon component (ui/js/react/index.tsx). Also add data-icon-kind to non-catalog icon kinds (emoji, text, typst, url/data image, raw svg, node, missing-placeholder) with their own closed animations so literally every icon animates. Remap the non-Lucide "glb" icon id to the vendored "box" icon via an alias. Extend ui.css with the keyframes, a single generic hover-trigger rule, and a prefers-reduced-motion guard. Extend the in-source vitest tests in ui/js/react/index.tsx to assert completeness (every icon id has a keyframes block + assignment) and closed-ness (0% frame equals 100% frame, except declared full-turn spin exceptions ending at +/-360deg). Extend the Icons storybook story with a hover-animation demo grid.
summary:
Third refinement pass per user feedback: "The microanimations must not be global animations but handcrafted for every svg... Make sure there are proper mechanisms and every icon is 100% specific."

Replaced every shared and misnamed keyframe with a bespoke, uniquely-named keyframe per icon. Before this pass, 31 keyframes were reused across ~70 icons (icon-commit-dot alone drove 27 different icons' pulses; icon-crosshair-* drove 25 nudges) and 36 more were unique but generically named. Now: 154/154 catalog icons animate, every animation name matches `icon-<id>` or `icon-<id>-<part>`, and no animation is referenced by more than one icon — enforced by three new tests (specificity, exclusivity, no-dead-keyframes) plus the pre-existing completeness/closedness tests, all reading directly from the real ui.css file.

Highlights of the individual tuning: git-commit's dot pings crisply while git-branch's tip lands softer and later (a commit arriving); the 4 focus brackets/layout-grid cells/combine boxes each got direction-specific corner keyframes instead of one shared shape; all ~20 crosshair-family directional nudges (move, hash, arrows, panels, undo/redo, chevrons, grid-3x3...) got their own amplitude/timing so an arrow's confident overshoot differs from a panel divider's soft slide; triangle-alert's exclaim pulses sharper than alert-circle's which pulses sharper than info's (urgency-graded, as sketched in the plan); sun's 8 rays shimmer independently from the disc's glow; users/user, smile's two eyes, and scissors/x each got asymmetric left/right or fast/slow variants instead of a mirrored pair.

Split table-2.svg's single fused path into 3 elements (frame + column divider + header divider) — verified mathematically exact (same absolute coordinates, same arcs, pixel-identical at rest) — so the header row now sweeps and the column divider nudges independently. Did NOT attempt the same for folder/folder-open: Lucide draws the tab as a notch in one continuous outline, not a separate closed shape, so a true split requires inventing new artwork (redrawing with a body shape + separate flap shape), which would change the icon's rest-state rendering — flagging this as a bigger decision the user can request separately rather than risking a silent visual regression to a shared vendored asset. Instead upgraded folder/folder-open to a skew-anchored-at-the-base motion (reads much more like "the flap tips" than a plain rotate) and gave message-square/message-circle a rotation pivoted at their tail tip (a speech bubble physically pivots there). Retuned wrench (origin at the jaw), check (origin at the tick's vertex), and moon (origin at its visual center of mass) to be explicit, geometry-derived mechanisms rather than arbitrary pivots.

All changes generated via scratch scripts with pre-write validation (closedness, exact-match dry-run splice, brace balance, postcss parse) — never hand-spliced. Final state: 154 unique icon rules, 0 duplicate keyframe names, 0 unresolved references, 0 specificity violations, 0 icons sharing an animation, 0 dead keyframes. All 10 icon tests pass; framework-renderer-react regression suite passes in full (240/240).

Storybook visual confirmation was attempted but blocked by the same environment-level dev-server streaming issue diagnosed in the prior pass (bundles fail mid-load in this session's Browser pane even against a confirmed-stable server process) — not related to these changes.
